land.text: the southern half of the divided Chenla, on 'the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia', linked to the Mekong Delta

predecessors.note: The Tang histories date the split 'shortly after 706', after 6 February 707; Cliopatria's row begins in 718.

land.text: 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page); 'much of the area fell under the orbit of the Shailendra dynasty of Srivijaya' (Jayavarman II page)

successors.note: The Javanese power is the Shailendra of Java/Srivijaya; Cliopatria also has a Mataram Kingdom row (741-1009). Jayavarman II ruled as the Javanese vassal 'King of Lower Chenla' c. 780-802 (his infobox).

land.text: the southern lands taken by Jayavarman II from Vyadhapura and Sambhupura up the Mekong; the Khmer Empire from 802

successors.note: Passes to the Khmer Empire only in 802, after twelve years of Javanese overlordship.

capitals.name: Vyadhapura / Baladityapura (site unidentified)
capitals.note: The page gives Pelliot's Vyadhapura and Coedes's Baladityapura (Aninditapura) for Water Chenla and does not locate either. The dot is the centre of Cliopatria's Water Chenla shape, not a site.

correction.text: The same outline, drawn from 707 to 789 (years only).

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 707-789, not 718-799. The split is c. 707 (Tang histories: after 6 February 707); the polity was 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790'. The 243,130 km2 outline (the Tonle Sap, the Mekong Delta, the Gulf coast) matches the page's 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia' and its link with the Mekong Delta; no km2 figure on the page.

correction.text: The same outline, but not a Water Chenla shape: Javanese-held 790-801, Khmer Empire from 802.

keyframe_review.note: Not Water Chenla's: the Chenla page says the last king 'seems to have been killed' and the polity was 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790'; the Jayavarman II page has Dharanindra's invasion killing Mahipativarman and the 'king of Zabag' installing Jayavarman II as vassal. The land is the Javanese dependency from 790 and Jayavarman II's Khmer Empire from 802, to be drawn from the suzerain's and the Khmer dossier.

region.text: the southern half of Chenla, on the Tonle Sap and the Mekong Delta

ledger.note: c. 707: Chenla splits and Water Chenla forms in the south. 'shortly after 706, the country was split into Land Chenla and Water Chenla' (New Book of Tang), after 6 February 707 by the Tang histories; 'Water Chenla is situated on the Tonle Sap area in Cambodia'.

region.text: the city of Kumbhupura in Kratié province, attacked by the Javanese in 780

ledger.note: 780: the Javanese strike Water Chenla. 'In 780, the Javanese Shailendra dynasty launched a naval attack on the city of Kumbhupura in Kratie province.' The page gives no year for Dharanindra's invasion that killed Mahipativarman; the 780 naval attack is its only dated Javanese blow.

region.text: the city of Kumbhupura in Kratié province, attacked by the Javanese in 780

ledger.note: c. 790: the Javanese hold ends the fighting. 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page infobox 'Javanese invasion: 790'); the Jayavarman II page puts Jayavarman II on the throne as the Javanese vassal.

c. 790: Water Chenla ends under Java. Its last king 'seems to have been killed' and the polity was 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790'. The Jayavarman II page instead has him 'King of Lower Chenla' c. 780-802 as a vassal of Java; the two pages are reconciled as a Javanese dependency, drawn in the suzerain's dossier, and the Khmer Empire from 802.

wars.name: Javanese (Shailendra) attack on Water Chenla (780-790)

zones.text: the city of Kumbhupura in Kratié province, attacked by the Javanese in 780

wars.outcome: A naval attack on Kumbhupura in 780; Mahipativarman killed; Water Chenla 'incorporated into the Javanese monarchy around the year 790' (Chenla page) with Jayavarman II as the Javanese vassal.
wars.note: The pages give only the 780 attack and the c. 790 incorporation; the years between are not dated.

wars.name: Jayavarman II's defeat of a Cham army (790)
wars.outcome: The Sdok Kak Thom inscription says Jayavarman II 'defeated a Cham army in 790'; the page names no place and no change of border. The Champa page records only Javanese raids on Champa in 774 and 787.
wars.note: Jayavarman II's standing in 790 is disputed between the two pages (Javanese vassal king of Lower Chenla).

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier; the Tonle Sap, Mekong Delta and Champa edges of the outline are approximate.

sources.title: Chenla
sources.note: Identity, the c. 707 split, Water Chenla on the Tonle Sap and Mekong Delta, the capital proposals, the Javanese incorporation c. 790, Jayavarman II's 790 victory over a Cham army. No km2 figure.

sources.title: Jayavarman II
sources.note: 780 Javanese naval attack on Kumbhupura (Kratie), Mahipativarman's death, Jayavarman II installed as Java's vassal, 'King of Lower Chenla c. 780-802'.

sources.title: Champa
sources.note: Opened for the Cham frontier: silent on Chenla; records Javanese or Kunlun raids on Champa in 774 and 787.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Water Chenla' row is the southern half of the Chenla of Wikidata Q1057118; written as its own state (see the chenla dossier's notes). Moved from Cliopatria: start 707 (not 718); end 790 (not 805), the Chenla page's date for incorporation into the Javanese monarchy. The Jayavarman II page conflicts: it gives him as King of Lower Chenla c. 780-802 under Java, so Water Chenla may have survived as a Javanese vassal to 802; unresolved, and reconciled by drawing 790-801 as the suzerain's dependency. Needs from other dossiers: srivijaya (Cliopatria row, other group) should carry a vassal_start (or gain) for water-chenla/Cambodia c. 780-790 and its end in 802; khmer-empire the gain of Water Chenla's land in 802. Whether the Javanese power is Srivijaya or Mataram is not settled by the pages. The capital is not located by the page (Vyadhapura/Baladityapura); the Seshat page (kh_chenla) was not opened.
